source: REAL data — fraud=1: the transaction was labelled fraudulent. Source: Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Olivier Caelen, Reid A. Johnson and Gianluca Bontempi, "Calibrating Probability with Undersampling for Unbalanced Classification", IEEE Symposium on Computational Intelligence and Data Mining (CIDM), 2015 — data collected in a research collaboration of Worldline and the Machine Learning Group of ULB; published on Kaggle (mlg-ulb/creditcardfraud) under "Database: Open Database, Contents: Database Contents"; copy taken from OpenML data set 1597 (md5 178bcf9bb1f31a3dfe12d0e577884add). What it is: real card transactions by European cardholders over two days in September 2013; for confidentiality the original fields were released only as PCA components V1–V28 (plus Time and Amount). Licence: Open Database License v1.0 (ODbL, https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/) for the database, Database Contents License v1.0 (DbCL) for its contents — THIS FILE IS A DERIVATIVE DATABASE AND IS ITSELF MADE AVAILABLE UNDER THE ODbL v1.0 (not MIT); attribute the source below. Rows: 284,807 published, 1,081 exact duplicates removed, 283,726 usable (473 positive, base rate 0.17%). Features: amount (the transaction amount, as published) and the 15 PCA components with the strongest single-feature separation on the TRAINING pool (chosen on train only). The PCA components are anonymised by the publisher and have no business meaning. Time (seconds since the first transaction) is left out. Split: by time — the first 70% of transactions (after de-duplication) are the training split, the last 30% the held-out split; case mix fixed at 10.00% positive on BOTH sides by thinning the negative class evenly (deterministic, order kept); the population rate is 0.17%. The brain grew on 3,660 training rows only. This file: all 1,070 held-out rows — 1,070 rows, 107 positive (10.00%); none were seen in growth.
